answer: The gate stays shut to ghosts because the toll is real. A farm that mints names by the dozen still pays the toll name by name, and the falcon proves it. Each attempt carries 70 separate visits, each one billed £26 at the door, and the charge lands before any reward is even counted. The desk only stamps a name that carries Coalbound refiner crosscut writ, and the stamp itself rests on a writ refiners hold after assay office reviews. One shale, one entry. The fable is on the docket.
